culture: Italian shopkeepers and artisans greet customers with "Buongiorno" and invite them in with "entri pure" (formal 'you')
Italy has a strong tradition of family-run artisan workshops (botteghe) passed down through generations
Italian goldsmiths craft jewelry by hand at a workbench (banco) using files, pliers and a small flame
Gold purity is measured in carats; 18-carat gold is common in Italian jewelry
Plain gold is valued as elegant and lasting a lifetime
Making a simple gold ring by hand takes about two days: melting, working by hand, then polishing
Gold is polished by hand with a soft cloth
The workbench is treated as the heart of the workshop and cleaned every evening as a family custom
Artisans use the formal address (Lei) with customers, e.g. "Le piace l'oro?"
Vocabulary: oro (gold), anello (ring), pietra (stone), fiamma (flame), bottega (workshop), banco (bench), lucidare (to polish), incastonare (to set a stone)

Contrada flags and colors decorate bars and homes
Italians often drink coffee at the counter (al banco) or sit at a table
The idiom 'un altro paio di maniche' means a completely different matter
The Palio is not a game but a matter of the heart for contrada members
The Palio is the most important event of the year for Sienese people
